=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh
Line or code reference: 337-346
Problem: The label `ai:merge-queued` is deleted via `gh_retry gh api -X DELETE` on line 337 BEFORE `_mt_dispatch_review "${num}" "${head}"` on line 339. When the dispatch fails, the PR has already lost its queue label. The `else` branch on line 344-345 logs only a warning and never re-adds the label. Since `_mt_release` on the release path skips PRs that lack the label (line 324: `_mt_has_label "${labels}" || continue`), the stranded PR is invisible to every future poll-tick release run.
Why it fails at runtime: A transient workflow-dispatch API failure leaves the PR unlabelled with no running review. For repos without the poller (core profile), no backstop re-dispatches the review and the PR stays unreviewed until a manual re-run. The last_commit_stat claims commit 030892f fixed this (label removed only after dispatch succeeds), but the working tree still has the old DELETE-before-dispatch order.
SEVERITY: BLOCKER
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- tests/test_review_merge_train.py
Line or code reference: 265-275 (test_release_keeps_label_when_dispatch_fails)
Problem: The test captures `_log_text` (the fake `gh` command audit log) but discards it via underscore naming convention (line 272). The test then asserts only `"could not be dispatched" in result.stdout` and `"MERGE_TRAIN_RELEASED" not in result.stdout`. It never inspects `log_text` for the presence or absence of the label DELETE call. Because the actual `scripts/review_merge_train.sh` deletes the label before attempting dispatch (see finding above), this test passes despite the exact bug it was written to catch.
Why it fails at runtime: The test gives false confidence. The label DELETE IS logged by the fake `gh`, but the test never reads the log. A correct test must assert that `log_text` does NOT contain `DELETE repos/acme/consumer/issues/4077/labels/ai%3Amerge-queued`.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- .github/workflows/cancel_on_pr_close.yml
Line or code reference: 215 (`if: github.event.pull_request.merged == true`)
Problem: The `Release merge-queued PRs (merge train)` step fires only when the closed PR was merged. A blocker PR closed without merging (e.g., closed manually or via `ai:closed`) does not trigger queue re-evaluation on `cancel_on_pr_close.yml`. The PR description documents this path as event-driven (immediate on merge), with the poll tick as the backstop. Core-profile consumer repos lack the poller.
Why it fails at runtime: In a core-profile repo, if an older overlapping `ai/issue-*` PR is closed without merging, every queued younger PR stays queued until a `pull_request.synchronize` event or a manual re-run fires on that specific PR — the `cancel_on_pr_close.yml` release step never runs. The gate re-check on the next synchronize event would clear the staleness, but if no new commits land on the queued PR, the gap persists indefinitely.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh
Line or code reference: lines 337-345 (the `gh_retry gh api -X DELETE` immediately followed by `if _mt_dispatch_review`)
Problem: The `ai:merge-queued` label is removed BEFORE the workflow-dispatch attempt. When `_mt_dispatch_review` returns non-zero, the PR is de-labelled but no review run has been queued, so the next `release` pass on the same base skips it via the `_mt_has_label "${labels}"` early-out (line 320). The warning on line 345 says "the next pull_request event or poll tick retries", but the label — which is the ONLY trigger for that retry — is gone. The LAST COMMIT message (030892f) explicitly claims this was fixed ("The label is now removed only after `gh workflow run` succeeds; on failure it stays"), but the actual code in the working tree still has the DELETE before the dispatch.
Why it fails at runtime: A first-attempt dispatch failure on any released PR (workflow file removed, transient GitHub API outage on `gh workflow run`, repo under temporary lock, etc.) silently drops the queue. The PR never runs review until a human removes-and-re-pushes or the queue is restarted by another merge event. This is the exact regression the LAST COMMIT was supposed to close (Copilot review discussion r3950859091).
SEVERITY: BLOCKER
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- .github/workflows/cancel_on_pr_close.yml
Line or code reference: lines 210-215 (the `Release merge-queued PRs (merge train)` step with `if: github.event.pull_request.merged == true`)
Problem: The release step only runs when `github.event.pull_request.merged == true`, so a blocker closed WITHOUT merge (e.g. closed as superseded, not planned, off-topic) does NOT trigger `release`. The `orchestrate_poll.yml` backstop only covers repos running the standard/full profile; the core workflow profile (workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt, listed in agents.md) ships `ai-cancel-on-pr-close.yml` but no `ai-orchestrate-poll.yml`, so core-profile consumers with a queued PR stuck behind a closed-not-merged blocker have no automated release path.
Why it fails at runtime: For core-profile consumers, queued PRs whose older blockers are closed-not-merged stay labelled `ai:merge-queued` indefinitely; no event handler and no scheduler picks them up. The PR's own review run is gated by the label, so review never resumes until a human manually removes the label and re-triggers. Even on standard/full profiles the merge-train release path loses the immediacy the workflow comment promises ("Re-evaluate the queue on this base right away") for any blocker that closed without merging.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh
Line or code reference: lines 344-346 (the `_mt_warn` branch when dispatch fails)
Problem: When dispatch fails after the label DELETE already happened (the bug above), the only audit line is the dispatch-failure warning. There is no log line correlating the missing `ai:merge-queued` label to the un-dispatched PR, so an operator scanning `MERGE_TRAIN_*` lines cannot tell which PRs were silently dropped by a failed dispatch versus genuinely still blocked.
Why it fails at runtime: After a transient GitHub outage or a workflow-file removal, the orchestrator loses queued PRs with no recoverable trail; the next `release` tick will only log `MERGE_TRAIN_RELEASE_SUMMARY examined=N released=M` with no per-PR signal explaining why expected `released` is less than `examined`.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
